Hi — pulling together the short-form answer we give to prospects (lean and definitive):

1) Default storage behavior (hosted API)
- Prompts / request payloads: by default, persistent request logs are retained for 30 days. These are used for billing/abuse detection and can be scoped by customer account or route.
- Model-generated outputs: considered "derived artifacts." By default we retain derived artifacts for 90 days to support debugging, regressions, and evals. Outputs are not surfaced to other tenants.
- Telemetry / service diagnostics (inference traces, kernel metrics): retained 90 days by default; aggregated and anonymized for product metrics.

2) Streaming responses
- Partial tokens emitted during a streaming session are transient by default. We only persist streaming fragments if the customer enables full-request logging or if the session is captured by a support trace. In normal operation streamed tokens are not materialized to persistent storage.

3) Residency / geography
- For traffic originating in EU regions using our EU endpoints, stored request and derived artifacts are kept in EU regions by default for the retention window above. We provide Proof-of-Residency logs on request for audits.

4) Immediate deletion / customer-initiated erasure
- Per-account or per-conversation immediate deletion is supported. Steps: (a) customer uses the Console "Delete Conversation" action or the Data Controls API endpoint; (b) we tombstone entries immediately (rendering them inaccessible) and schedule backend purge jobs; (c) purge completes within 72 hours for typical requests. Legal holds or enterprise compliance preserves tombstones per policy until released.

5) How customers reduce retention
- Console toggles and the Data Controls API let customers reduce the default retention window (min 7 days for billing/abuse reasons) or opt-out of retaining derived artifacts entirely. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) do not forward logs to Redwood's hosted telemetry by default.

6) Exceptions and evidence
- We will retain a minimal audit trail when required for forensic/abuse investigations, and anything preserved for legal reasons is marked and excluded from normal purge flows.

I've attached the retention_matrix_v2.xlsx that maps all artifact classes to windows and the runbook for deletion SLAs. Karthik, please add anything I'm missing from the infra/TTL side.

Adding infra specifics / clarifications from the runtime side:

- Auto-purge mechanics: items are tombstoned immediately at deletion request, then queued into the purge pipeline which processes per-shard batches. Standard pipeline completes within 72 hours; customers with enterprise SLA can request a 24-hour expedited purge.
- Cache layers: prefix/KV caches are held in-memory and evicted per LRU; we do not treat transient KV cache evictions as "deletions" because they are ephemeral and not part of persistent retention counts.
- EU residency enforcement: for hosted EU accounts we pin storage to EU-only buckets; cross-region replication is disabled unless the customer enables disaster-recovery (explicit opt-in).
- API flags: Data Controls API supports "retain_artifacts": [full|minimal|none] and "force_purge": true to trigger expedited purge. Note that "none" will still preserve minimal billing/abuse metadata for 7 days.

Alex — short answers and links below.

1) Streaming fragments: yes. If a customer requests deletion of a conversation that includes mid-stream fragments, our Data Controls API/Console deletes all materialized fragments tied to that conversation. Non-persisted in-memory fragments never hit persistent stores and require no action.

2) Backups / snapshots: standard backups are retained up to 30 days by default and are on a separate retention schedule. The 72-hour purge window refers to primary persistent stores; we surface an expedited purge option for enterprise customers where backup retention can be shortened to align with the requested purge (this requires a signed SLA amendment and may incur additional charges).

Runbook: attached immediate-delete-runbook.pdf (short procedural checklist + request templates).

If BrightBank would like, I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the deletion runbook and evidence package (SOC2 artifact pointers, residency proofs).
